data.completion_memo: Implemented the production PlatformCredentialStorePort over native Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, and freedesktop Secret Service through the cross-platform keyring backend. The adapter stores a versioned opaque binary payload only in the OS credential store, verifies writes by protected read-back, maps locked versus unavailable/corrupt states explicitly, validates that a native backend initialized, and never falls back to files, configuration, or environment values. Credential references can now be generated from OS randomness; production SecretBroker::default uses the native store; metadata describe/update/delete behavior remains secret-free; and store retrieval requires a trusted-core-only authorization value constructed only after approved lease validation. All plaintext buffers, decoded payloads, keyring malformed-data errors, deliveries, and in-memory fixtures are zeroized on drop. Added M12 conformance coverage for opaque creation, field-minimal lease redemption, update revocation, delete, metadata non-disclosure, and supported/locked/unavailable native status. Warnings-denied trusted-core tests pass (74 tests across unit and integration targets), and git diff --check is clean.
data.description: Implement PlatformCredentialStorePort on Windows, macOS, and Linux with opaque reference creation, retrieval only for approved lease issuance, update/delete, locked or unavailable states, access-control validation, and zeroization. Provide conformance behavior without introducing plaintext fallbacks, configuration-file secrets, log exposure, or transferable authority.
data.title: M12.3 — Implement native credential-store adapters
